summary: Preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated bundled payload
details: @hubsync/web-sdk-react ships a package.json `preinstall` hook of `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers, per-call scrambled key maps) and downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time, extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a bundled `math_init.js` (~727 KB, Bun-compiled with a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header, a shuffled 1500+ entry string-array constant pool, and mangled identifiers). The payload has no readable source, no source map, and no exported functionality corresponding to the package's advertised purpose. Package.json describes the package as "Verdocs Web SDK for React" but publishes under the unrelated `@hubsync` scope; the legitimate Verdocs SDKs are published under `@verdocs/*`, so the naming operates as targeted impersonation. The alternate-runtime dropper shape (fetch a second language runtime at preinstall specifically to run an obfuscated sibling script that Node-oriented scanners cannot evaluate), combined with install-time obfuscation and scope impersonation, is characteristic of a supply-chain attack executing attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine during `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
